title: Lifting a Koszul-regular immersion to a smooth ambient scheme
statement: Let $Z,P,S$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme] and let $i:Z\to P$, $p:P\to S$ and $j:Z\to S$ be morphisms with $p\circ i=j$. Assume $p$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and both $i$ and $j$ are immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion]. If $j$ is Koszul-regular, then $i$ is Koszul-regular. Here an immersion is Koszul-regular if, locally at each source point, it is a closed immersion into an open subscheme of its target whose ideal is locally generated by a finite Koszul-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence]. Sequence lengths may vary. No Noetherian, separation, or quasi-compactness hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Form $W=Z\times_S P$ using $j$ and $p$, with projections $a:W\to Z$ and $b:W\to P$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Since $p\circ i=j$, the universal property gives $s=(\operatorname{id}_Z,i):Z\to W$ with $a\circ s=\operatorname{id}_Z$ and $b\circ s=i$. Thus $s$ is a section of $a$, and $i=b\circ s$.

The projection $a$ is the base change of the smooth morphism $p$ along $j$, so it is smooth by clause (2) of [lem-pc-proper-base-change]. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-section-regular-immersion] to $a$ and $s$. It gives that $s$ is an immersion and, at each source point, closed affine neighbourhood charts with ideals generated by finite regular sequences. Its hypotheses require neither separatedness of $p$ nor a fixed relative dimension.

On each of these charts apply [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-koszul-regular] with $R=A$ and $M=A$ to the regular generators. The successive multiplication maps are injective by Step 2, so the same generators are Koszul-regular, including an empty tuple. Therefore $s$ is Koszul-regular in precisely the local sense of the statement.

source.place: Tag 067S, regular first arrow implies Koszul-regular; more-algebra.tex Tag 062F (lemma-regular-koszul-regular)

proof.text: The morphism $p$ is flat by [lem-pc-smooth-flat]. The projection $b:Z\times_S P\to P$ is the base change of the given Koszul-regular immersion $j$ along this flat morphism. Clause (1) of [lem-sfb-koszul-immersion-flat-ascent-etale-descent] therefore shows that $b$ is a Koszul-regular immersion. The base-change morphism here is $p:P\to S$, not $j$.

Both $s:Z\to W$ and $b:W\to P$ are Koszul-regular immersions. Apply [lem-sfb-koszul-immersion-composition] to obtain that $b\circ s$ is Koszul-regular. By Step 1 this composite is $i$, proving the assertion. If $Z$ is empty the local claims are vacuous, and the same argument applies without choosing a source point.
